_comment: Scenario: UC-01 fatigue/drowsiness — long friend drive (M2 behavioral engine).
M2 design: drowsiness grows at base=0.9/min + monotony=0.3/min = 1.2/min on
normal_road (monotonous segments).  Initial state: drowsiness=0 (none),
fatigue=60 (high — exhausted from short night's sleep before a long drive).
Proposal timeline (tick_seconds=60, 60 kph on normal_road → 1 km/tick;
tick N advances to elapsed=N+1 min, distance=N+1 km):
Ticks 0-10:  drowsiness ≤ 13.2 (none band) → NO_TRIGGER
Tick 11:     drowsiness = 14.4 (none→weak at 20), fatigue_level=high boosts blend
Ticks 11-28: drowsiness in [none,weak), aw 0-16 → SOFT_WARNING via high-fatigue blend
Tick 29:     drowsiness = 36.0 (weak, aw=18), fatigue=68.7 (high)
damped blend ≥ 3.0  →  declarative_rule fires REST_PROPOSAL
rest spot at 60 km, distance=30 km → 30 min ahead (far, reachable)
Tick 50:     drowsiness = 61.2 (moderate, aw≈39), fatigue=75.3 (high)
base_safety_risk = 0.512 ≥ 0.45 (min_risk)
rest_required_score = 0.620 ≥ 0.62 (threshold_suggest)
rest spot at 60 km, distance=51 km → 9 min ahead (actionable)
weighted_score fires REST_PROPOSAL (gentle)
Exactly ONE REST_PROPOSAL per package across the run.  The run pauses; user accepts rest.
Note: event_presets.signal_duration_at_trigger is retained (required field) but
is not used by the M2 tick engine; the signal_duration ordinal is derived
from drowsinessAboveWeakTicks by build_feature_groups in binning.py.

persona.name: Haruto Tanaka
persona.description: A 35-year-old office worker on a long interstate drive to visit a friend. Started mid-afternoon after a very short night's sleep; fatigue is already high at departure.

review_focus: UC-01 fatigue/drowsiness (M2): verify profile-driven fatigue+drowsiness progression fires exactly one REST_PROPOSAL — declarative_rule at tick ~29 (high fatigue boosts blend to ≥ 3.0, rest spot 30 min ahead), weighted_score at tick ~50 (base_safety_risk ≥ 0.45 gates rest bonus, rest_required ≥ 0.62, rest spot 9 min ahead) — with all prior ticks as SOFT_WARNING or NO_TRIGGER.
